title: Both figure scripts write the identical 5 PNG filenames to the same dir - last run wins, can silently ship fabricated figures
description: generate_figures.py (RESULTS_DIR='./ICONS_M7/results', PLOT_DIR=results/plots, lines 10-11) and generate_figures_3seed.py (lines 28-29) both save the SAME five basenames (fig1_accuracy_comparison.png, fig2_forgetting.png, fig3_gate_trajectory.png, fig4_memory_efficiency.png, fig5_architecture_schematic.png) into the SAME directory. Legacy writes at 82/118/149/181/250; corrected writes at 179/222/276/326/376. Whichever runs last overwrites the other under identical names. generate_figures.py draws every data panel from hardcoded/fabricated numbers and needs no CSV, so running it last (or at all) silently replaces the corrected CSV-sourced figures with fabricated ones bearing the trusted filenames. Neither file namespaces or version-stamps its output.
fix: Retire/delete generate_figures.py (superseded by generate_figures_3seed.py). If kept, write to a clearly-marked separate dir (e.g. plots_LEGACY_FABRICATED/) with renamed outputs. Consolidate on one generator.

title: No __main__ guard: importing generate_figures.py renders and writes all 5 fabricated figures (needs no CSV)

Unlike generate_figures_3seed.py it reads NO CSV - all data is hardcoded - so `import generate_figures` (or any tool importing it to inspect) unconditionally creates ./ICONS_M7/results/plots/ (line 12) and writes fig1..fig5 built from fabricated numbers, with no error and no input required. This is the most dangerous import in the cluster: it always succeeds at producing fabricated research output.

title: POSITIVE: dedup is correct (one row per seed+condition); minor: .first() is first-non-null-per-column, not 'first row'

description: FRAME_ELEMS['dvs'] = 25*2*34*34 (294) uses the POOLED 34x34 resolution (comment: 'pooled 128->34 to match the visual backbone'), but the bar it feeds is labeled 'Raw dense frames (50/class)' (313). title: aggregate() computes mean/std over ALL numeric columns (incl. seed and all-NaN step); re-validate under pinned pandas 3.0.2
description: sub.mean(numeric_only=True) (88) and sub.std(numeric_only=True, ddof=1).fillna(0.0) (89) reduce over every numeric column, which includes 'seed' (mean-of-seeds is meaningless) and the all-NaN 'step' column (mean/std -> NaN, std filled to 0). Currently harmless because m()/s() only read named accuracy/forgetting columns, but it is sloppy and could surface if a numeric column is later treated as a metric. requirements.txt pins pandas==3.0.2; pandas 3.0 changed several reduction/string-dtype defaults, so this reduction path (and ddof=1 single-row -> NaN -> fillna(0) for single-seed) should be re-validated on the pinned version. Low confidence on any specific 3.0 breakage; flagged for verification.
fix: Select the metric columns explicitly before mean/std (drop 'seed'/'step'), and add a smoke test under pandas 3.0.2.

title: Expected seed set {42,123,456} hardcoded in the plotting script

But it is a second copy of the seed policy that can drift from the training script.

title: Summary-row mask at line 65 is fragile: KeyError if 'step' absent; nullable-boolean mask risk under pandas 3.0 string dtype
description: summary = df[df['step'].isna() | (df['step'].astype(str).str.strip()=='')].copy() (65). Two fragilities: (1) if the CSV lacks a 'step' column, df['step'] raises KeyError with no friendly message - the dual-schema contract is assumed, not checked. (2) Under pandas 3.0 (pinned 3.0.2), if 'step' is inferred as the new string dtype rather than float, str.strip()=='' yields a nullable BooleanArray; OR-ing/masking that with possible <NA> can raise 'Cannot mask with non-boolean array containing NA'. In practice blank CSV cells usually parse to float NaN (safe path), so this is conditional - confidence low - but worth a guard.
fix: Guard for the 'step' column's presence and coerce the mask to plain numpy bool (fillna(False) / .to_numpy(dtype=bool)) before indexing.

title: box() helper and the entire Figure 5 architecture schematic are duplicated across both figure scripts
description: The box() helper (generate_figures.py 192-197 vs generate_figures_3seed.py 339-343) and the whole Figure-5 schematic block (generate_figures.py 185-252 vs generate_figures_3seed.py 330-378) are near-identical copies. title: '95% CI' computed as mean +/- 1.96*std - missing /sqrt(n); mislabeled statistic
description: Line 289 prints a '95% CI' as [mean - 1.96*std, mean + 1.96*std]. A 95% CI for the mean is mean +/- 1.96*std/sqrt(n) (normal approx) or mean +/- t_{.975,n-1}*s/sqrt(n). The /sqrt(n) factor is missing, so with n=5 the reported interval is ~sqrt(5)=2.24x too wide and is NOT a CI of the mean - it is roughly a coverage/spread interval for individual observations. Compounding: spinnaker_accs.std() (288) uses numpy default ddof=0 (population std, not sample), and 1.96 (z) is used where t_{.975,4}=2.776 fits n=5. Any number copied from this line into the paper as a '95% CI' would be a mislabeled statistic.
fix: Compute CI as mean +/- t.ppf(0.975, n-1) * s/sqrt(n) with s = ddof=1 sample std; or relabel the interval as an observed spread. Use ddof=1 for the reported std too.

title: Accuracy reported without spike rate / sparsity - violates 'accuracy never travels alone'
description: The PyTorch baseline accuracy (pt_acc, computed 251, printed 252/283) and the SpiNNaker-sim accuracies (spinnaker_accs mean/std/CI, 286-289) are reported with NO spike-rate or sparsity metric. The simulator accumulates head spike counts (s3_acc, 147/179) and tracks all-zero samples (zero_count/total_zero_count, 182/271/291) but never computes or reports network spike rate or sparsity. Timestep count is partial - DURATION_MS=100 (100 steps) is printed for the sim (202/285) - but the PyTorch baseline's timestep count (T from data, ~25 for N-MNIST) is not reported. Per research-integrity.md an SNN accuracy without its spike-rate/sparsity and timestep cost is the part of the result that flatters us.
evidence: pt_acc / spinnaker_accs printed with no spikes/sparsity
fix: Report mean spikes/neuron (or spike rate) and sparsity for both sim and baseline alongside accuracy, and state the timestep count for each; the sim already has s3_acc and could accumulate per-layer spike totals cheaply.

title: 'SpiNNaker-deployed network' overclaim and unsourced Brian2-equivalence claim in the file's prose
description: The docstring (line 3) says 'the corrected SpiNNaker discrete-time simulator', but the printed HONEST STATEMENT escalates to 'the final, locked evaluation of the SpiNNaker-deployed network' (303) and claims it 'uses the EXACT IF_curr_exp parameters from build_spinnaker_network() and was verified against raw Brian2 to produce identical argmax predictions on 20 stratified reference samples' (306-308). Per CLAUDE.md/spinnaker.md nothing has run on a board (HARDWARE_ACCESS_CHECKLIST entirely unchecked); this is a CPU discrete-time SIMULATOR, so 'SpiNNaker-deployed' conflates simulation with deployment (Mapping != inference != real hardware). build_spinnaker_network() is neither defined nor imported here, and no Brian2 comparison runs in this file (Brian2 not imported), so the '20 stratified reference samples' equivalence is asserted as fact without any in-file/in-repo artifact. The corresponding verify_brian2_raw.py lives in code/archive/, not here.
evidence: 'evaluation of the SpiNNaker-deployed network' + 'verified against raw Brian2 ... 20 stratified reference samples'
fix: Reword to 'discrete-time simulator of the mapped parameters' and drop 'deployed'. Either reproduce the Brian2 comparison and cite its output artifact, or remove the specific 20-samples/identical-argmax claim; do not state cross-simulator equivalence as fact without a sourced artifact.

title: SEEDS=[42,123,456,789,999] deviates from project policy [42,123,456]
description: SEEDS = [42, 123, 456, 789, 999] (26) adds 789 and 999 beyond the documented policy set {42,123,456} (m7_trimodal_run.py:516). Nuance: here the seeds vary ONLY the Poisson input-encoding RNG (run_spinnaker_sim seed, 104) for a FIXED network and FIXED SCALE - not model init or data shuffling - so this is an input-noise ensemble, a legitimately different axis from the training-seed policy. Still worth flagging: (a) inconsistent with the documented seed set and invites conflation, and (b) n=5 feeds the mislabeled CI (FIG-018), lending it false authority.
fix: Either align to the documented seeds or add a comment stating these are input-encoding seeds (distinct from training seeds) and why 5 were chosen; keep the two seed concepts clearly separated in any reported number.

title: torch.load of a missing checkpoint crashes the only run path; CWD-relative path; name lacks seed
description: main() calls torch.load('ICONS_M7/results/checkpoints/final_nmnist_nmnist_replay.pt', map_location='cpu') (207). The repo has NO checkpoints, so the script raises FileNotFoundError immediately - the entire evaluation depends on this file. The path is CWD-relative (no './'; resolves only from code/, and note it uses 'ICONS_M7/...' whereas the figure scripts use './ICONS_M7'). The filename 'final_nmnist_nmnist_replay.pt' also lacks the seed field of the documented pattern final_{task}_{task}_seed{seed}_{condition}.pt. Unlike generate_figures_3seed.py (which sys.exits with guidance on a missing CSV), this gives a bare traceback. Minor: torch.load is called without weights_only=; torch 2.11 (pinned) defaults weights_only=True (secure-by-default), which also means a non-tensor-only checkpoint would fail here.
fix: Check the path exists and emit an informative message (mirror the CSV-missing pattern); make the path './ICONS_M7/...'; confirm the intended checkpoint filename/seed convention; pass weights_only explicitly.

title: collect_stratified silently under-collects if a class has <200 samples; assumes batch_size=1; KeyError if label>=10
description: collect_stratified (88-99) fills up to per_class (200) samples/class, breaking early once all classes are satisfied (97-98). If any class has fewer than per_class samples in the loader, the all(...) condition never becomes True and the loop simply exhausts the finite loader and returns fewer samples than requested - with NO error - while main() still prints '200/class' (200/223). It also assumes batch_size=1 via int(y.item()) (92) - y.item() raises if a batch has >1 element (batch_size=1 is set at 221, so this is a coupled assumption). counts is keyed 0..9 (90); a label >=10 would KeyError. Not an infinite loop (the for-loop is bounded by the finite loader).
evidence: counts = {i: 0 for i in range(10)}; break when all(c >= per_class ...)
fix: After the loop, assert each class reached per_class (or report actual per-class counts); derive the class set from the data rather than hardcoding range(10); document the batch_size=1 requirement.

title: Headline accuracy depends on hand-tuned SCALE=7.0 and other magic scale factors whose calibration is not in-repo
description: The reported sim accuracy is sensitive to several hand-set scalars: SCALE=7.0 (27, applied to weights at 120), RATE_SCALE=10.0 (28, applied at 111), bias*10.0 (123), and probs=rates/1000.0 (112). The docstring/statement assert SCALE 'was calibrated once and never adjusted' (8/304), but the calibration procedure and its target are not present in this file or (per repo context) in any CSV, so the choice of 7.0 is an undocumented researcher degree-of-freedom that directly moves the headline number. These are also undocumented magic constants (with DURATION_MS=100 at 29, refrac_steps=2 at 134, thresholds -50/-65, tau 20/5 at 130-133).
fix: Document how SCALE=7.0 (and the *10 bias / rate scaling) were calibrated, against what metric and data, ideally with a sourced artifact; name the LIF magic constants and cite build_spinnaker_network() as their single source.

title: argmax over all-zero head spike counts silently predicts class 0
description: preds = np.argmax(head_counts, axis=1) (183). For any sample with zero total head spikes, head_counts row is all zeros and np.argmax returns index 0 - the sample is silently classified as class 0, biasing accuracy/confusion toward class 0. zero_count (182) records how many such samples occur and the report prints the total (291), but the predictions still default to 0 rather than being marked no-prediction. The HONEST STATEMENT relies on 'Confirms 0 all-zero' - if that count is ever nonzero, accuracy already silently absorbed those as class-0 guesses.
evidence: preds = np.argmax(head_counts, axis=1) with zero_count tracked separately
fix: Mark all-zero samples as an explicit no-prediction sentinel (e.g. -1) and exclude/flag them in accuracy and confusion, instead of letting argmax default to class 0.

title: mean_confusion_matrix computes a single (non-mean) CM; dead 'p>=0' guard; transposed cm[pred,true] orientation
description: mean_confusion_matrix (187-192) computes counts for ONE seed's predictions, not a mean - the averaging happens later at np.mean(spinnaker_cms, axis=0) (276) - so the name is misleading. The guard `if p >= 0` (190) is dead: p comes from np.argmax and is always >=0 (see FIG-025 - all-zero rows still yield 0, never negative). cm[p, t] += 1 (191) stores [predicted, true], the transpose of the conventional cm[true, pred]; the print loop labels rows r and columns by class index (294-297), so a reader assuming sklearn convention would misread rows/columns.
evidence: def mean_confusion_matrix(...): if p >= 0: cm[p, t] += 1
fix: Rename to confusion_matrix; drop the dead p>=0 guard (or make it meaningful once no-prediction sentinels exist, FIG-025); document the [pred,true] orientation or switch to [true,pred].

title: code/ script reaches into the legacy bi-modal package via sys.path hack
